subtitle: Charred tomato salsa
verso: No salsa, no taco; and no molcajete, no salsa.
story: Charred on the comal and ground in the volcanic-stone molcajete. Chunky, smoky, and on the table at every meal.

ingredients.title: Salsa
items: ¼ white onion, in one piece

steps: Heat a dry comal or cast-iron pan over medium-high. Char the tomatoes, chiles, garlic and onion, turning, until blistered and soft: about 8 minutes for the garlic and chiles, 12–15 for the tomatoes.
Peel the garlic and grind it with salt in the molcajete into a paste. (If you used chiles de árbol, toast them only a few seconds; they burn fast.)
Add the chiles and grind them. Add the tomatoes one at a time and crush, then the onion.
Thin with a little water and keep it chunky. Taste for salt.
No molcajete? Pulse a few times in a blender. Don't purée.
pressureNote: No pressure-cooker version. Salsas come off the comal in minutes.
tips: Season a new molcajete by grinding a handful of raw rice in it, again and again, until the rice comes out white instead of gray.

variations.name: Salsa Verde Cocida
variations.subtitle: Cooked tomatillo salsa
variations.note: The everyday green salsa for tacos, carnitas and chilaquiles.
steps: Simmer the tomatillos and chiles 8 minutes, until olive green.
Blend with the garlic, onion, cilantro, salt and a few spoons of the cooking water.

variations.name: Salsa de Chile de Árbol
variations.subtitle: Taquería árbol salsa
variations.note: The thin, fiery red salsa from the taquería.
steps: Toast the chiles in a dry pan 30 seconds, stirring, until fragrant. Don't let them blacken.
Blend everything until smooth. Strain if you want it silky.
